# pkgdiff

> Shows every release note between two versions of a package across NuGet, npm, PyPI, Maven, pub.dev and Packagist in one categorized timeline, with a security picture of the upgrade.

pkgdiff helps developers decide whether a dependency upgrade is safe. It combines release notes from the registries and from GitHub, and adds vulnerability and project health data. It is free to use and needs no account.

## Main pages

- [Home](https://pkgdiff.dev/): Search for a package in any supported registry
- [Browse packages](https://pkgdiff.dev/packages): All packages pkgdiff has analyzed
- [Dependency audit](https://pkgdiff.dev/audit): Check a manifest's dependencies for known problems
- [About](https://pkgdiff.dev/about): Who runs pkgdiff, its data sources and their limits

## Packages by registry

- [NuGet packages](https://pkgdiff.dev/packages?registry=nuget)
- [npm packages](https://pkgdiff.dev/packages?registry=npm)
- [PyPI packages](https://pkgdiff.dev/packages?registry=pypi)
- [Maven packages](https://pkgdiff.dev/packages?registry=maven)
- [pub.dev packages](https://pkgdiff.dev/packages?registry=pub.dev)
- [Packagist packages](https://pkgdiff.dev/packages?registry=packagist)

## Package pages

Package pages follow the pattern `https://pkgdiff.dev/package/{registry}/{packageId}`, for example [react on npm](https://pkgdiff.dev/package/npm/react). Each one lists the package's versions with categorized release notes, and can compare two versions.

## Data sources

- Registries: NuGet, npm, PyPI, Maven Central, pub.dev and Packagist
- Release notes: registry pages, GitHub releases and changelogs
- Security: OSV.dev, deps.dev, OpenSSF Scorecard and Socket

Changes are categorized by rules that match release note headings and keywords, so a category can be wrong. The release digests under `/blog` are AI-generated and not reviewed by a person; do not treat them as a primary source.
